frank: Heads-up: onboarding smoke for `kestrel-14b-int4v3` on staging (48k ctx) shows a reproducible integrity glitch right after a kvcache reanchor at ~12288 tokens — not a pure prob drop, decoder emits an unexpected separator token sequence and then recovers. filing here before i open the MR.

lucy: separator token sequence? any minimal repro or log snippet?

frank: minimal repro below — run tests/prefill_scan.py with flags. observed in 4/6 runs.

```
# reproduce
python tests/prefill_scan.py --model kestrel-14b-int4v3 --prefill 13000 --seed 21 --ctx 49152 --log-level debug
```

omar: log excerpt: 
```
[2025-09-12T10:12:10Z] prefill.start id=pf-4c9a tokens=13000
[2025-09-12T10:12:31Z] kvcache.reanchor shard=0 old_window=8192 new_window=12288 reanchor_ts=1765559987
[2025-09-12T10:12:31Z] rope.reanchor_apply delta=0.0009 kernel=quant4v3
[2025-09-12T10:12:31Z] decode.token 12285 tok=... prob=0.045
[2025-09-12T10:12:32Z] decode.token 12296 tok=<SEP><SEP> prob=0.0012  <-- double-sep emission
[2025-09-12T10:12:33Z] decode.token 12305 tok=... prob=0.043  <-- recovery
```

quant-bot: quick stat: in failing traces the double-<SEP> appears 3x more often for int4v3 than int8/fp16 around reanchors. see QLAB-519 for similar observations in smaller scope.

lucy: interesting. does toggling the reanchor path change behavior? try `--disable_reanchor=true` or `--rope_reanchor_safe_guard=true`.

frank: tried `--disable_reanchor=true` and the double-<SEP> disappears (5/5 clean). with default reanchor it's 4/6 failing.

omar: is this specific to int4v3 kernels? have you tried int4v2, int8, fp16?

frank: quick matrix: fp16 -> clean; int8 -> rare single <SEP> spike; int4v2 -> infrequent; int4v3 -> consistent double-<SEP>.

ops-bot: scheduling a small sweep on staging as requested: job=staging-prefill-6122 matrix=[fp16,int8,int4v2,int4v3] runs=6 flags=[KV_LOG_EXTRA=1,ROPE_REANCHOR_DEBUG=1,KVCACHE_PAGE_HASH_VERBOSE=1] ETA ~10m.

ci-bot: job 6122 queued by frank. artifacts will be at https://ci.internal/reports/6122/longprefill.log

lucy: two plausible causes: (A) reanchor applies a small index delta and int4v3's dequantization rounding produces two nearby high-prob tokens (separator) because of packing stride effects; (B) kvcache reanchor writes a transient marker row that the decoder interprets as extra separater tokens when page read and rescale interleave.

omar: i can try a local microbench: pack/unpack roundtrip at page-aligned offsets with int4v3 to see if ordering is preserved. also will add a quick spectral diff of 12270-12320 with reanchor on/off.

frank: i'll attach the token diff CSV and minimal trace in the MR. also adding `--kvcache-sync-commit=true` as an option to test atomic commits.

quant-bot: note: int4v3 uses a new pack stride=12 optimization; QLAB-519 suggests stride==page_size alignment can amplify rounding artifacts.

lucy: if this is quant packing amplification of tiny rescale deltas, immediate mitigation: gate reanchor for int4v3 on staging (safe default off) until we patch safe-guard. Add longprefill boundary checks at 8k,12k,16k to onboarding checklist.

frank: agreed. plan: 1) wait for staging sweep results; 2) if sweep confirms int4v3-only, open hotfix PR to disable reanchor for int4v3 on onboarding runners and add telemetry; 3) longer term patch pack/unpack memcpy ordering and add a tiny clamp in reanchor that avoids producing sign changes for separator tokens.

omar: ping me when you upload diffs. i'll run the microbench and link results here.

ci-bot: job 6122 started. logs will appear at https://ci.internal/reports/6122/

frank: thanks all  i'll open MR with traces + diffs and tag @lucy @omar for review. please ping if you want early access to staging logs. :thumbsup:
